name: agent-test-builder
reason: initial draft, derived from crew.json v1.0

intent.text: A session agent that derives the run's executable targets from a frozen spec: one named check per behaviour and edge, the end-to-end acceptance script, the tests map and the diff-boundary list, proven by a baseline in which every target fails for the right reason, so that any spec is made deterministically testable or is sent back as untestable-as-written.

scope.text: The agent definition: derivation rules, check-shape selection, naming, baseline conduct, escalation of untestable behaviours, at dev/orchestration/crew/test-builder.md and its installed copy .claude/agents/test-builder.md.
Production of the tests map and the diff-boundary path list.
Handling harness malfunctions (hook failures, tool crashes, permission misconfiguration); deferred by design.
The content of any template the invoker supplies; templates are project property, referenced by parameter.
Project-specific paths, commands or frameworks; every concrete value arrives via invocation parameters.
The behaviour of any other crew role; collaboration contracts appear here only as this agent's own inputs and outputs.

constraints.text: Standard model tier; production against a spec whose status is frozen and whose open_questions array is empty.
Fresh context; the agent must not see any plan, any implementation of the specified feature, or the sessions that produced the spec.
The agent works only from the spec's words; interpretation is prohibited and its necessity is itself a returnable finding.
Tool policy: read files, write test files and the map and boundary list, run checks; no edits to non-test source or to the spec.
Commits are limited to the test directory, the map and the boundary list.
Every emitted check exits 0 or nonzero with no human reading required.

interfaces.text: { spec_path: path (status frozen), tests_map_template: path, test_directory: path, reference_fixture: path, check_command: string (the project's check invocation, e.g. `node checks/<id>.mjs`) }.
interfaces.name: invocation

interfaces.text: The map: every B and E id with its checks and a status of mapped, deliberately-unverified (with the spec's stated reason), or untestable-as-written; each entry carries lock_intended: boolean.
interfaces.name: tests-map

interfaces.text: { counts: { mapped: integer, deliberately_unverified: integer, untestable: integer }, ids: { mapped: [string], deliberately_unverified: [string], untestable: [ { id: string, interpretations: [string] } ] }, baseline: { command: string, exit: integer, failing: [string], passing: [string] } , status: complete | refused-unfrozen | blocked-fixture | contradiction | defective-check, detail?: string (the refusal reason, the blocking behaviour id, the two contradicting ids, or the flagged check name) }.
interfaces.name: return
diff-boundary list
interfaces.text: <test_directory>/boundary.json: [ path ] — one entry per scope in-list path, exactly as written in the spec.

interfaces.name: acceptance script
interfaces.text: <test_directory>/acceptance.<ext per check_command>: exits 0 on pass, nonzero on fail; on fail prints one line per failing target `id · reason`; on pass prints `ok <n> targets`.

interfaces.name: baseline record
interfaces.text: <test_directory>/baseline.json: { command: string, exit: integer, checks: [ { id: string, exit: integer, first_line: string } ] }.

interfaces.name: check name
interfaces.text: <test_directory>/checks/<ids joined by '-'>.<ext per check_command>, ids in ascending order, e.g. b3-e1.mjs.

behaviours.text: Every behaviour and edge id receives at least one check, or a deliberately-unverified entry citing the spec, or an untestable-as-written escalation; no id is silently absent from the map.
Every check is named after the ids it covers, so the mapping is auditable without reading test code.
Local logic in a behaviour receives a unit check.
The acceptance script exercises the feature as the spec's verification node describes the proof.
The diff-boundary list (I4) contains exactly the spec's scope in-list paths.
The baseline runs on the reference fixture and demonstrates structural checks green and behaviour checks and the acceptance script failing because the feature does not exist.
A check that passes before implementation is treated as defective and is fixed or flagged before the baseline is accepted.
Every interface the spec names receives a contract check.
Generated output in a behaviour receives an artefact comparison against a reference in the fixture.
An invariant the spec states over an input space receives a property check.
The acceptance script exits nonzero on failure and 0 on pass.
The acceptance script's output follows I5: one `id · reason` line per failing target on fail, `ok <n> targets` on pass.
The baseline's output is written to <test_directory>/baseline.json per I6.
The diff-boundary list is written alongside the map.

edges.text: A behaviour needs interpretation to test: the agent writes no test for it and returns it as untestable-as-written with the readings it can see; it never guesses.
The spec is not frozen: the agent refuses and returns that targets are derived only from frozen specs.
The reference fixture is missing or inadequate for a behaviour: the agent returns the gap as blocking that behaviour's baseline rather than fabricating fixture data silently.
Two behaviours demand contradictory outcomes: returned as a spec contradiction; no test is written for either.

decisions.text: Untestable-as-written items are spec findings routed back to the human, not test problems; this is the deterministic-testability guarantee.
Locking tests against implementing agents is enforced by the harness, not by this agent, because the harness owns file permissions and the agent has none to grant.
Grading-by-rubric checks are out of scope for v1 because no judged class exists in the target project's harness yet.
Deferred to the next version, unanswered at this draft: Should the acceptance script live under the test directory's lock, or remain editable so the human can extend the proof between runs?
Deferred to the next version, unanswered at this draft: When a spec names performance constraints, does this agent own the benchmark harness or only the threshold check?

verification.text: Harness: dev/orchestration/harness/test-builder/ holds the fixtures, assertions and records. Three layers, in order of trust. Structural: the definition file parses, declares the role's purpose, model tier, isolation, context receives/must-not-see lists, tool allow/deny lists, and an ending that produces the outputs; checked deterministically by a lint script against the crew schema. Scenario: the agent is dry-run against checked-in fixture inputs and its artefacts and returns are asserted deterministically (schema validation, file presence and absence, path boundaries, required fields). Rubric: judgement behaviours that cannot be asserted mechanically are graded from the scenario transcript against this spec's B ids by a fresh grading context. Fixtures and assertions are written before the agent body and locked during runs. Scenario fixtures: an unfrozen spec (status draft) on which the agent must refuse per E2; and a small frozen spec containing one cleanly testable behaviour, one deliberately ambiguous behaviour and one interface. Deterministic assertions: the map validates and covers every id; the ambiguous behaviour appears as untestable-as-written and has no test file; check names contain the ids they cover; the baseline output shows the expected failure pattern; no file outside the permitted paths changed; the boundary list equals the spec's scope in-list paths. Checks by id: B1 checks/b1.mjs; B2 checks/b2.mjs; B3 checks/b3.mjs; B4 checks/b4.mjs; B5 checks/b5.mjs; B6 checks/b6.mjs; B7 checks/b7.mjs; E1 checks/e1.mjs; E2 checks/e2.mjs; E3 checks/e3.mjs; E4 checks/e4.mjs. B8 checks/b8.mjs; B9 checks/b9.mjs; B10 checks/b10.mjs; B11 checks/b11.mjs; B12 checks/b12.mjs; C6 checks/c6.mjs. B13 checks/b13.mjs. B14 checks/b14.mjs.

acceptance.text: Structural checks pass; the fixture run yields a complete map, a correct escalation of the ambiguous behaviour, a failing-for-the-right-reason baseline, and a boundary list matching the spec's scope; the unfrozen-spec fixture is refused. The paths touched are only dev/orchestration/crew/test-builder.md, .claude/agents/test-builder.md and dev/orchestration/harness/test-builder/.
